predecessors.name: Duchy of Bohemia
predecessors.text: the Brno, Olomouc and Znojmo principalities merged into the Margraviate in 1182

successors.name: Czechoslovakia
successors.text: In 1918 the Margraviate became 'Moravia Land' and later 'Moravia-Silesia Land'; its autonomy was eliminated in 1949

rulers.name: Rudolph I of Germany (direct royal rule)

ledger.x: 1182: Emperor Frederick Barbarossa has the Margraviate of Moravia created.
1310: the House of Luxembourg takes the margraviate.
1423: Albert V of Austria, Sigismund's son-in-law, becomes margrave (table 1423-1439); the first Habsburg margrave since Rudolf I of Habsburg in 1306-1307.
1479: the Peace of Olomouc ends the contest; Matthias renounced the royal title (of Bohemia) and, the page says, retained the rule over the Moravian lands.
1479-1490: Moravia is held by Matthias Corvinus as margrave (table 1468-1490).
1490: Vladislaus II of Bohemia (Jagiellon) succeeds Matthias Corvinus as margrave.
1641: the capital moves from Olomouc to Brno (infobox: Olomouc 1182-1641, Brno 1641-1918); no sentence in the text describes the move.
1918: the Margraviate of Moravia ends (infobox 'Disestablished: 1918') and becomes Moravia Land in Czechoslovakia; its autonomy was eliminated in 1949.

wars.name: Hungarian occupation of Moravia and the Peace of Olomouc
wars.outcome: Matthias Corvinus occupied Moravia in 1469; the 1479 Peace of Olomouc settled the dispute, Matthias renouncing the royal title (of Bohemia) and retaining the rule over the Moravian lands.

wars.name: Ottoman raids on Moravia
wars.outcome: Moravia was frequently raided; the page says hundreds of thousands were enslaved and tens of thousands killed.

certainty.note: The page gives no boundary line or treaty; Moravia is a long-lived land named by its three founding principalities and Cliopatria's outline is approximate.
